I1.quote: Searched main text and SI for a gravimetric, volumetric or flow H2 uptake measurement; none found. Uptake of 2 H2 by the Rh6 cluster is shown only by ESI-MS; the 0.1 % w/w capacity is stoichiometric.

I5.quote: Hydrogen storage is an area of intense current interest, which is driven by the requirements for reversible storage of dihydrogen for future energy applications.

notes: Molecular rhodium hydride cluster [Rh6(PCy3)6H12][BArF4]2 (A) adds 2 H2 to give B; uptake is shown by ESI-MS (SI, p. 3, 'Procedure for the storage / release cycle': 'ESI-MS shows uptake of 2 H2 to give [Rh6(PCy3)6H16][BArF4]2 B'). The stated 'hydrogen storage capacity of A (0.1 % w/w)' (main, p. 4) matches 2 H2 per cluster formula unit, not a gravimetric/volumetric/flow uptake value. This is a reaction of H2 (oxidative addition to a cluster) without a measured uptake, so I1 fails; storage is from H2 gas, not charging in an electrolyte (only the redox-triggered release is followed by cyclic voltammetry), so the I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated rather than electrochemical; the paper reports experiments, so not theoretical_only. If I1 were met, I2 would also fail: the sorbent is a molecular metal-hydride cluster salt, not a carbon sorbent in any schema class. No surface area is reported. Primary communication with data; not retracted; the earlier report of H2 addition to A (ref. [21]) is cited but the paper does not state that all its uptake values were published before.
